# D-Sentry wire protocol

> Generated from `D-SentryCode/protocol/protocol_spec.py` by `D-SentryCode/tools/gen_protocol.py`. The same file produces
> `protocol/dsentry_protocol.h` (and its byte-identical ESP32 copy
> `firmware/UNOR4USBBridge/dsentry_protocol.h`) and `relay-pc/dsentry/protocol.py`, so the
> C, Python and this page cannot drift. `gen_protocol.py --check` fails while any is stale.
> The contract behind it is `docs/architecture.md` section 4.

## Framing

Every packet travels as `start | len | payload[len] | crc`. `len` is the number of payload bytes: everything after len, excluding crc. All multi-byte fields are
little-endian; field names are identical in C (`dsentry_protocol.h`), Python (`protocol.py`) and here.

A receiver accepts a frame only when:

1. the first byte is one of the four start bytes;
2. len equals that packet type's exact payload length (never a range);
3. the CRC over len and the payload matches the crc byte;

and on any mismatch the deframer drops only the first held byte and searches again from the next one, so a frame hidden inside a rejected candidate is still found.

Why the exact length: ASCII debug text shares the USB port with binary frames. StatusPacket's start byte 0x5A is the letter 'Z'; it is safe only because its len byte (7) is a control character that text never contains. Research measured 0 false frames in 2 MB of random printable text with the exact-length rule, and about 1 in 256 candidates accepted when any length was allowed.

**CRC:** CRC-8/SMBUS, width 8, poly `0x07`, init `0x00`, no input or output reflection, xor-out
`0x00`; check value over ASCII `123456789` = `0xF4`. It covers the len byte and the payload (every byte after start, before crc).

| Packet | Start | len | Frame bytes | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ControlPacket](#controlpacket) | `0xA5` | 10 | 13 | Controller input (spec 5) |
| [StatusPacket](#statuspacket) | `0x5A` | 7 | 10 | Turret status and rumble requests (spec 5, plus rumbleSeq) |
| [TelemetryPacket](#telemetrypacket) | `0xD5` | 107 | 110 | Everything the dashboard shows |
| [BeaconPacket](#beaconpacket) | `0xD6` | 8 | 11 | WiFi discovery |

Constants:

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DS_PROTO_VERSION` | 1 | D-Sentry protocol version; `AT+DSCAPS?` reports it as dsProto. |
| `DS_TELEMETRY_VERSION` | 2 | TelemetryPacket.version; a receiver that sees another value must not trust the fields. |
| `DS_ANGLE_SCALE` | 100 | Wire units per degree. Angles are centidegrees (deg * 100), angular rates centidegrees/s. |
| `DS_TELEMETRY_LCD_ROWS` | 2 | Rows of the LCD mirrored in TelemetryPacket.lcd. |
| `DS_TELEMETRY_LCD_COLS` | 16 | Characters per mirrored LCD row (space padded). |
| `DS_PAD_BATTERY_UNKNOWN` | 255 | TelemetryPacket.padBattery when the source reports no level (= XBOX_R4_BATTERY_UNKNOWN). |
| `DS_MAX_FRAME_LEN` | 110 | largest frame of any packet (deframer buffer size) |

## ControlPacket

Start `0xA5`, len 10, frame 13 bytes. Controller input (spec 5). Stick up is negative (the Bluepad32/SDL convention); the RA4M1 applies JOY_INVERT_Y.

- PC relay -> ESP32 by UDP to WIFI_UDP_PORT at CONTROL_PACKET_HZ, always sent (connected = 0 when there is no input source) so the ESP32 knows where to reply.
- PC (relay or bench console) -> RA4M1 over USB serial, accepted only when DEBUG_ACCEPT_USB_CONTROL; wins over the radio while fresh.
- the ESP32 does not forward it raw: in WiFi mode it turns the latest valid one into the 20-byte `AT+XBOXSTATE?` state the RA4M1 polls.

| Frame offset | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | start | u8 | `0xA5` |
| 1 | len | u8 | 10 |
| 2 | `flags` | u8 | DS_CTRL_FLAG_* bits (see ControlFlags) |
| 3-4 | `rx` | i16 | right stick X, -512..511, right positive |
| 5-6 | `ry` | i16 | right stick Y, -512..511, up negative |
| 7-8 | `rt` | u16 | right trigger, 0..1023 |
| 9-10 | `buttons` | u16 | DS_BTN_* bits (see Buttons) |
| 11 | `seq` | u8 | increments per packet, wraps; the RA4M1 counts gaps and echoes it in TelemetryPacket.lastCtrlSeq |
| 12 | crc | u8 | CRC-8 over bytes 1-11 |

**Worked example.** These values:

| Frame bytes | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `a5` | start | |
| `0a` | len | 10 |
| `03` | `flags` | 0x03 (connected, sourceWifi) |
| `00 fe` | `rx` | -512 |
| `ff 01` | `ry` | 511 |
| `ff 03` | `rt` | 1023 |
| `11 08` | `buttons` | 0x0811 (a, lb, back) |
| `07` | `seq` | 7 |
| `ac` | crc | |

encode to this 13-byte frame:

<!-- example ControlPacket -->
```text
a5 0a 03 00 fe ff 01 ff 03 11 08 07 ac
```

## StatusPacket

Start `0x5A`, len 7, frame 10 bytes. Turret status and rumble requests (spec 5, plus rumbleSeq).

- RA4M1 -> PC over USB serial, on change and every STATUS_HEARTBEAT_MS.
- ESP32 -> PC relay by UDP (WiFi mode), to the source of the last valid ControlPacket, so the relay rumbles the pad it holds.
- RA4M1 -> ESP32 carries the same values as `AT+DSS` arguments, not as a frame.

| Frame offset | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | start | u8 | `0x5A` |
| 1 | len | u8 | 7 |
| 2 | `wantMode` | u8 | radio the RA4M1 wants (mirrors the A1 toggle) (see RadioMode) |
| 3 | `rumbleStrong` | u8 | strong (low-frequency) motor, 0..255 |
| 4 | `rumbleWeak` | u8 | weak (high-frequency) motor, 0..255 |
| 5-6 | `rumbleMs` | u16 | rumble length in ms; 0 = stop |
| 7 | `state` | u8 | turret state (see TurretState) |
| 8 | `rumbleSeq` | u8 | increments on every new rumble command, so a heartbeat repeat is not a new shot |
| 9 | crc | u8 | CRC-8 over bytes 1-8 |

**Worked example.** These values:

| Frame bytes | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `5a` | start | |
| `07` | len | 7 |
| `01` | `wantMode` | 1 (WIFI) |
| `c8` | `rumbleStrong` | 200 |
| `78` | `rumbleWeak` | 120 |
| `50 00` | `rumbleMs` | 80 |
| `05` | `state` | 5 (ARMED) |
| `2a` | `rumbleSeq` | 42 |
| `9f` | crc | |

encode to this 10-byte frame:

<!-- example StatusPacket -->
```text
5a 07 01 c8 78 50 00 05 2a 9f
```

## TelemetryPacket

Start `0xD5`, len 107, frame 110 bytes. Everything the dashboard shows. Start byte >= 0x80 so it is never ASCII. Pan: positive = counter-clockwise seen from above (stick right turns the turret clockwise, i.e. negative; PAN_DIR_INVERT fixes the hardware side). Tilt: 0 = calibrated bottom plus backoff, positive = barrel up.

- RA4M1 -> PC over USB serial every 1000/TELEMETRY_USB_HZ ms.
- RA4M1 -> ESP32 as `AT+DST=<hex>` every 1000/TELEMETRY_WIFI_HZ ms in WiFi mode; the ESP32 forwards the bytes unchanged by UDP to the relay.

| Frame offset | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | start | u8 | `0xD5` |
| 1 | len | u8 | 107 |
| 2 | `version` | u8 | DS_TELEMETRY_VERSION |
| 3 | `seq` | u8 | increments per TelemetryPacket, wraps |
| 4-7 | `uptimeMs` | u32 | RA4M1 millis() when built |
| 8 | `state` | u8 | turret state (see TurretState) |
| 9 | `fault` | u8 | fault code (see Fault) |
| 10 | `fireMode` | u8 | 0 semi, 1 full (see FireMode) |
| 11 | `linkSource` | u8 | active control source (see LinkSource) |
| 12-13 | `flags` | u16 | DS_TELEM_FLAG_* bits (see TelemetryFlags) |
| 14-17 | `panCdeg` | i32 | pan position, centidegrees, + = CCW from above |
| 18-21 | `tiltCdeg` | i32 | tilt position, centidegrees, + = up |
| 22-23 | `panVelCdegS` | i16 | pan velocity, centidegrees/s |
| 24-25 | `tiltVelCdegS` | i16 | tilt velocity, centidegrees/s |
| 26-29 | `homePanCdeg` | i32 | stored home pan, centidegrees |
| 30-33 | `homeTiltCdeg` | i32 | stored home tilt, centidegrees |
| 34 | `ammo` | u8 | darts left |
| 35 | `magCapacity` | u8 | MAG_CAPACITY |
| 36-37 | `shotsTotal` | u16 | strokes completed since boot, wraps |
| 38 | `flywheelDuty` | u8 | ENA duty now, 0..255 |
| 39 | `servoDeg` | u8 | trigger servo commanded angle, degrees |
| 40-41 | `stallSample` | u16 | latest A2 reading, ADC counts |
| 42-43 | `stallBaseline` | u16 | stall EMA baseline, ADC counts |
| 44-45 | `stallPeak` | u16 | largest \|sample - baseline\| of the current or last move, ADC counts |
| 46-47 | `loopHz` | u16 | loop() iterations per second, saturates |
| 48-49 | `ctrlRxHz` | u16 | valid control frames per second from the active source |
| 50-51 | `crcErrors` | u16 | control-path CRC errors since boot, wraps |
| 52-53 | `seqGaps` | u16 | control seq gaps since boot, wraps |
| 54-55 | `stepJitterPermille` | u16 | worst step jitter of the last stats window, permille of the step period |
| 56 | `lastCtrlSeq` | u8 | seq of the last accepted ControlPacket (echo for round-trip latency) |
| 57 | `espMode` | u8 | radio the ESP32 reports (see EspMode) |
| 58 | `ledR` | u8 | LED 0 red as sent, after the brightness clamp |
| 59 | `ledG` | u8 | LED 0 green as sent |
| 60 | `ledB` | u8 | LED 0 blue as sent |
| 61-92 | `lcd` | char[32] | LCD text, row 0 then row 1, space padded |
| 93 | `padState` | u8 | **v2:** controller connection state (see PadState) |
| 94 | `padBattery` | u8 | **v2:** pad battery percent 0..100 (`AT+XBOXSTATE?` byte 17), 255 = unknown |
| 95-96 | `padLx` | i16 | **v2:** left stick X, -512..511, right positive (BLE only, else 0) |
| 97-98 | `padLy` | i16 | **v2:** left stick Y, -512..511, up negative (BLE only, else 0) |
| 99-100 | `padRx` | i16 | **v2:** right stick X as received, right positive |
| 101-102 | `padRy` | i16 | **v2:** right stick Y as received, up negative |
| 103-104 | `padLt` | u16 | **v2:** left trigger, 0..1023 (BLE only, else 0) |
| 105-106 | `padRt` | u16 | **v2:** right trigger as received, 0..1023 |
| 107-108 | `padButtons` | u16 | **v2:** DS_BTN_* levels as received, bits 12-15 included (see Buttons) |
| 109 | crc | u8 | CRC-8 over bytes 1-108 |

**Versions.** This is version 2 (`DS_TELEMETRY_VERSION`); fields marked **vN** were appended by version N.
A version 1 frame ends after `lcd`: len 91, frame 94 bytes.
The PC side reads the older layouts too (`Deframer(accept_legacy=True)`, which the relay and the bench console use; the missing fields keep their defaults and `version` says which layout arrived), so a relay keeps working with an older RA4M1 build. The C deframer, the RA4M1 and the ESP32's `AT+DST` check accept the current layout only.

**Worked example.** These values:

| Frame bytes | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `d5` | start | |
| `6b` | len | 107 |
| `02` | `version` | 2 |
| `c8` | `seq` | 200 |

## BeaconPacket

Start `0xD6`, len 8, frame 11 bytes. WiFi discovery. The relay listens on WIFI_DISCOVERY_PORT when no --udp host is given.

- ESP32 -> UDP broadcast on WIFI_DISCOVERY_PORT every WIFI_BEACON_MS while in WiFi mode.

| Frame offset | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | start | u8 | `0xD6` |
| 1 | len | u8 | 8 |
| 2-5 | `ip` | u8[4] | the turret's IPv4 address, first octet first (192.168.4.1 = c0 a8 04 01) |
| 6-7 | `udpPort` | u16 | where to send ControlPackets (WIFI_UDP_PORT) |
| 8 | `bootId` | u8 | random non-zero byte chosen at ESP32 boot |
| 9 | `mode` | u8 | WiFi status: 2 station, 3 own AP, 4 relay heard (see WifiStatus) |
| 10 | crc | u8 | CRC-8 over bytes 1-9 |

**Worked example.** These values:

| Frame bytes | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `d6` | start | |
| `08` | len | 8 |
| `c0 a8 04 01` | `ip` | 192.168.4.1 |
| `72 10` | `udpPort` | 4210 |
| `5c` | `bootId` | 92 |
| `03` | `mode` | 3 (AP_UP) |
| `e0` | crc | |

encode to this 11-byte frame:

<!-- example BeaconPacket -->
```text
d6 08 c0 a8 04 01 72 10 5c 03 e0
```

## Enums

Each is one byte on the wire. C: `#define` with the prefix shown and `ds_turret_state_name()`-style name functions;
Python: an `IntEnum` of the same name.

### TurretState

Top-level state of the RA4M1 state machine (spec 3.1, architecture.md 6). C prefix `DS_STATE_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `OFF` | power toggle open: steppers disabled, flywheel 0, servo detached, LEDs dark |
| 1 | `BOOT` | peripherals starting; lasts one tick after begin() |
| 2 | `CALIBRATING` | tilt homing |
| 3 | `PAIRING` | waiting for a connected control source |
| 4 | `DISARMED` | connected; motion allowed, trigger and flywheels locked |
| 5 | `ARMED` | connected; flywheels and firing allowed |
| 6 | `FAULT` | calibration or stall fault (see Fault) |

### Fault

Why the turret is in FAULT (TelemetryPacket.fault). C prefix `DS_FAULT_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `NONE` | no fault |
| 1 | `CAL` | calibration failed; clears only by toggling power |
| 2 | `STALL` | stall detected; clears after STALL_FAULT_HOLD_MS |

### RadioMode

Radio the RA4M1 wants the ESP32 to run (StatusPacket.wantMode, `AT+DSS` wantMode). Mirrors the BT/WiFi toggle on A1. C prefix `DS_RADIO_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `BLE` | the turret pairs directly with the pad over BLE |
| 1 | `WIFI` | the PC relay holds the pad and sends ControlPackets over UDP |

### EspMode

Radio the ESP32 reports running (`AT+DSS` reply espMode, TelemetryPacket.espMode). C prefix `DS_ESP_MODE_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `BLE` | BLE client running |
| 1 | `WIFI` | WiFi station or access point running |
| 2 | `NONE` | no D-Sentry radio started yet |
| 3 | `RESTARTING` | the other radio was running; the ESP32 stored the wanted mode and restarts into it about 50 ms after this reply |
| 255 | `UNKNOWN` | RA4M1 side only: no DSS reply yet, or legacy firmware |

### LinkSource

Which input the RA4M1 is obeying (TelemetryPacket.linkSource). USB wins while a valid USB ControlPacket arrived within LINK_TIMEOUT_MS (architecture.md 4.3). C prefix `DS_LINK_SRC_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `NONE` | no live source |
| 1 | `BLE` | the pad over BLE, through `AT+XBOXSTATE?` |
| 2 | `WIFI` | the PC relay over UDP, through `AT+XBOXSTATE?` |
| 3 | `USB` | ControlPackets over the USB serial port (bench override) |

### PadState

Controller connection state (TelemetryPacket.padState). BLE source: the `AT+XBOXSTATE?` state byte (byte 16, enum xbox_r4_conn_state in protocol/xbox_r4_protocol.h) as sent; WiFi source: the same byte, which the ESP32 sets to 0 or 3; USB source: 0 when the ControlPacket says connected, else 3. C prefix `DS_PAD_STATE_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `CONNECTED` | reports flowing (BLE), or the source says connected (WiFi, USB) |
| 1 | `WAITING_FIRST_REPORT` | BLE link up, encryption or subscription in progress |
| 2 | `FOUND` | BLE: the pad was seen in a scan, connecting |
| 3 | `SCANNING` | BLE: no pad connected, scanning; WiFi or USB: the source is not connected |
| 4 | `OFF` | BLE: the ESP32's Xbox client is not running |
| 5 | `BLOCKED_BY_HCI` | BLE: the ArduinoBLE HCI bridge owns the radio until `AT+RESET` |
| 255 | `NONE` | no control source: no frame arrived within LINK_TIMEOUT_MS |

### FireMode

Trigger behaviour, toggled by B (TelemetryPacket.fireMode). C prefix `DS_FIRE_MODE_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `SEMI` | one stroke per pull |
| 1 | `FULL` | strokes back-to-back while the trigger is held |

### WifiStatus

ESP32 WiFi state (`AT+DSS` reply wifiStatus, BeaconPacket.mode). C prefix `DS_WIFI_STATUS_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `OFF` | WiFi not running |
| 1 | `CONNECTING` | station connecting |
| 2 | `STATION_UP` | joined WIFI_SSID as a station |
| 3 | `AP_UP` | hosting its own access point WIFI_AP_SSID |
| 4 | `RELAY_HEARD` | a valid ControlPacket arrived from the relay within LINK_TIMEOUT_MS |

### DstResult

`AT+DST` reply. C prefix `DS_DST_`.

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `NOT_SENT` | not forwarded: not in WiFi mode, no relay address yet, or the hex was not exactly one valid TelemetryPacket |
| 1 | `SENT` | forwarded by UDP to the relay |

## Bit masks

C: `#define <prefix><KEY>` = `1 << bit` (plus `<prefix>ALL`). Python: an `IntFlag` of the same
name, and `BIT_KEYS` / `bits_to_dict()` for the camelCase keys below.

### ControlFlags

ControlPacket.flags. 8 bits, C prefix `DS_CTRL_FLAG_`.

| Bit | Mask | Key | C macro | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `0x01` | `connected` | `DS_CTRL_FLAG_CONNECTED` | a controller (pad or keyboard) is live; 0 = neutral input, no source |
| 1 | `0x02` | `sourceWifi` | `DS_CTRL_FLAG_SOURCE_WIFI` | source: 0 = BLE, 1 = WiFi (the relay) |
| 2 | `0x04` | `espPairing` | `DS_CTRL_FLAG_ESP_PAIRING` | the ESP32 is in pairing mode |
| 3 | `0x08` | `keyboard` | `DS_CTRL_FLAG_KEYBOARD` | the relay's dashboard keyboard is driving, not a pad |

### Buttons

ControlPacket.buttons and TelemetryPacket.padButtons (spec 3.2 mapping: A arm, B semi/full, X magazine, d-pad left set home, d-pad down go home). Bits 12-15 exist for the dashboard's controller view: a ControlPacket may carry them and the RA4M1 never acts on them. 16 bits, C prefix `DS_BTN_`.

| Bit | Mask | Key | C macro | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `0x0001` | `a` | `DS_BTN_A` | A: toggle ARMED/DISARMED |
| 1 | `0x0002` | `b` | `DS_BTN_B` | B: toggle semi/full |
| 2 | `0x0004` | `x` | `DS_BTN_X` | X: reset magazine to MAG_CAPACITY |
| 3 | `0x0008` | `y` | `DS_BTN_Y` | Y: unused |
| 4 | `0x0010` | `lb` | `DS_BTN_LB` | left bumper: flywheels |
| 5 | `0x0020` | `rb` | `DS_BTN_RB` | right bumper: unused |
| 6 | `0x0040` | `dpadUp` | `DS_BTN_DPAD_UP` | d-pad up: unused |
| 7 | `0x0080` | `dpadDown` | `DS_BTN_DPAD_DOWN` | d-pad down: go home |
| 8 | `0x0100` | `dpadLeft` | `DS_BTN_DPAD_LEFT` | d-pad left: set home |
| 9 | `0x0200` | `dpadRight` | `DS_BTN_DPAD_RIGHT` | d-pad right: unused |
| 10 | `0x0400` | `start` | `DS_BTN_START` | Menu (start): unused |
| 11 | `0x0800` | `back` | `DS_BTN_BACK` | View (back): unused |
| 12 | `0x1000` | `lsClick` | `DS_BTN_LS_CLICK` | left stick click: shown on the dashboard, no turret action |
| 13 | `0x2000` | `rsClick` | `DS_BTN_RS_CLICK` | right stick click: shown, no turret action |
| 14 | `0x4000` | `xbox` | `DS_BTN_XBOX` | Xbox (guide) button: shown, no turret action |
| 15 | `0x8000` | `share` | `DS_BTN_SHARE` | Share button: shown, no turret action |

### TelemetryFlags

TelemetryPacket.flags. 16 bits, C prefix `DS_TELEM_FLAG_`.

| Bit | Mask | Key | C macro | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `0x0001` | `linkConnected` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_LINK_CONNECTED` | a control source is connected |
| 1 | `0x0002` | `flywheelOn` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_FLYWHEEL_ON` | flywheel commanded on (ramping or at duty) |
| 2 | `0x0004` | `flywheelReady` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_FLYWHEEL_READY` | flywheel on for at least FLYWHEEL_SPINUP_MS |
| 3 | `0x0008` | `strokeActive` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_STROKE_ACTIVE` | a trigger stroke is in progress |
| 4 | `0x0010` | `triggerPulled` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_TRIGGER_PULLED` | trigger reads pulled (hysteresis applied) |
| 5 | `0x0020` | `homing` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_HOMING` | a go-home position move is running |
| 6 | `0x0040` | `calibrated` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_CALIBRATED` | tilt calibration finished; tilt bounds active |
| 7 | `0x0080` | `powerToggleOn` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_POWER_TOGGLE_ON` | power toggle (A0) reads on |
| 8 | `0x0100` | `modeToggleWifi` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_MODE_TOGGLE_WIFI` | mode toggle (A1) reads WiFi |
| 9 | `0x0200` | `stallEnabled` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_STALL_ENABLED` | stall detector active |
| 10 | `0x0400` | `emptyMagBlink` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_EMPTY_MAG_BLINK` | empty-magazine blink showing |
| 11 | `0x0800` | `driversEnabled` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_DRIVERS_ENABLED` | stepper drivers enabled (EN low) |
| 12 | `0x1000` | `espLegacyFirmware` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_ESP_LEGACY_FIRMWARE` | the ESP32 answered `AT+DSCAPS?` with ERROR (old fork/stock) |
| 13 | `0x2000` | `lcdPresent` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_LCD_PRESENT` | an LCD answered on I2C |
| 14 | `0x4000` | `espAlive` | `DS_TELEM_FLAG_ESP_ALIVE` | the ESP32 answered within LINK_TIMEOUT_MS |

### Caps

`AT+DSCAPS?` capBits: what the ESP32 firmware supports. 8 bits, C prefix `DS_CAP_`.

| Bit | Mask | Key | C macro | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `0x01` | `rumble` | `DS_CAP_RUMBLE` | rumble in BLE mode (`AT+DSS` rumble fields reach the pad) |
| 1 | `0x02` | `wifi` | `DS_CAP_WIFI` | WiFi mode (station/AP, UDP ControlPackets) |
| 2 | `0x04` | `mode` | `DS_CAP_MODE` | radio switching through `AT+DSS` wantMode |
| 3 | `0x08` | `telemetry` | `DS_CAP_TELEMETRY` | `AT+DST` forwarding to the relay |

## AT commands (RA4M1 <-> ESP32, Serial2 at LINK_BAUD)

Served by the ESP32 fork's chAT server next to the existing Xbox commands. Every command
answers with its prompt and `OK` (`+NAME: ...\r\nOK\r\n`); failures go in the payload, never
a bare `ERROR`, because the RA4M1 would only notice that at its timeout. Arguments and reply
fields are decimal unless the type says hex. C names: `DS_AT_<ID>` (the `+NAME` string),
`DS_AT_<ID>_ARGC`, `DS_AT_<ID>_ARG_<NAME>` (argument index), `DS_AT_<ID>_REPLY_COUNT`,
`DS_AT_<ID>_REPLY_<NAME>` (reply field index).

| Command | Reply | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AT+DSCAPS?` | `+DSCAPS: <dsProto>,<capBits>` | Capability probe. The old fork and stock firmware answer a bare ERROR: the RA4M1 then treats the ESP32 as legacy (BT mode only, `AT+XBOXBEGIN` when the state says OFF). |
| `AT+DSS=<wantMode>,<rumbleSeq>,<strong>,<weak>,<rumbleMs>,<state>` | `+DSS: <espMode>,<bootId>,<wifiStatus>` | Status: the StatusPacket fields as decimal arguments. The ESP32 starts the wanted radio (idempotent). If the other radio is running it replies espMode = 3, stores the wanted mode in RTC_NOINIT memory, restarts about 50 ms later and boots straight into it. A new rumbleSeq triggers rumble: BLE mode -> the pad (client task, 0x2A4D output report); WiFi mode -> a StatusPacket by UDP to the relay. Sent when its content changes or every STATUS_HEARTBEAT_MS. |
| `AT+DST=<hex>` | `+DST: <sent>` | Telemetry. WiFi mode forwards the bytes unchanged by UDP to the relay. The line is 7 + 2 * TelemetryPacket frame length + 2 bytes; the RA4M1 writes Serial2 directly (D-Sentry never uses the WiFiS3 Modem, whose 127-byte line limit would cut it), and chAT accepts arguments of 5000 hex characters (research test_at_limits.cpp). |

### `AT+DSCAPS?`

| Reply field | Name | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `dsProto` | u8 | the firmware's DS_PROTO_VERSION |
| 1 | `capBits` | u8 | DS_CAP_* bits |

Example (12 request bytes on the wire):

```text
-> AT+DSCAPS?\r\n
<- +DSCAPS: 1,15\r\nOK\r\n
```

### `AT+DSS=<wantMode>,<rumbleSeq>,<strong>,<weak>,<rumbleMs>,<state>`

| Arg | Name | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `wantMode` | u8 | DS_RADIO_*: radio to run |
| 1 | `rumbleSeq` | u8 | StatusPacket.rumbleSeq; a new value starts the rumble below |
| 2 | `strong` | u8 | StatusPacket.rumbleStrong, 0..255 |
| 3 | `weak` | u8 | StatusPacket.rumbleWeak, 0..255 |
| 4 | `rumbleMs` | u16 | StatusPacket.rumbleMs; 0 = stop |
| 5 | `state` | u8 | DS_STATE_*: turret state, for the ESP32's own log |

| Reply field | Name | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `espMode` | u8 | DS_ESP_MODE_*: radio running now (3 = restarting into wantMode) |
| 1 | `bootId` | u8 | random non-zero byte chosen at ESP32 boot; a change means it rebooted |
| 2 | `wifiStatus` | u8 | DS_WIFI_STATUS_* |

Example (26 request bytes on the wire):

```text
-> AT+DSS=1,42,200,120,80,5\r\n
<- +DSS: 1,92,4\r\nOK\r\n
```

### `AT+DST=<hex>`

| Arg | Name | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `hex` | hex | one complete TelemetryPacket frame (start..crc), 2 hex digits per byte |

| Reply field | Name | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `sent` | u8 | DS_DST_*: 1 = forwarded by UDP to the relay, 0 = not |

Example (229 request bytes on the wire):

```text
-> AT+DST=d56b02c840e2010005000101c7683aeeffffd2040000d8dc0000000000002c0100000c0f030071140002fe0107009426640002000100230007007f2f0041524d454420462020414d4d4f3a313242542020202020436f6e6e656374656400508000d4fe00feff010002ff031160ca\r\n
<- +DST: 1\r\nOK\r\n
```

### Existing fork commands D-Sentry uses

Wire format in `protocol/xbox_r4_protocol.h` and the repo root's `docs/protocol.md`.

| Command | Reply | D-Sentry use |
|---|---|---|
| `AT+XBOXSTATE?` | `+XBOXSTATE: 20\|<20 bytes>` | Controller state, polled every 1000/CONTROL_PACKET_HZ ms in both modes. In WiFi mode the fork builds it from the relay's latest valid ControlPacket (state 0 when connected and fresher than LINK_TIMEOUT_MS, else 3 scanning). |
| `AT+XBOXBEGIN` | `+XBOXBEGIN: <code>` | Legacy firmware only: start the BLE client whenever a state frame says OFF, rate-limited by LINK_BEGIN_RETRY_MS. |
| `AT+SOFTRESETWIFI` | `OK` | Never sent by D-Sentry. The fork turns it into a prompt+OK no-op while a D-Sentry radio mode is active, because it would tear WiFi down. |
